Theme

Money, work & business · Civic life: news, government & the law

president noun

the head of a society, a club or a company

also chairman, chairwoman, club president, company president, head of a society, superintendent

classical

Cic. Planc. 32: maximārum societātum auctor, plūrimārum magister
M-O s.v. corporation: president of a corporation: societātis magister
Traupman 289

magister, magistrī m.

noun, second declension

the head of a company, a society or a guild

Lewis & Short: a master, chief, head, director, president. Cicero’s word for the head of a company of tax-farmers (societās); Morgan–Owens uses it for the president of a corporation.

Other words

  • praeses, praesidis m./f. — one who presides; a president

    noun, third declension, masculine or feminine · also used · classical · Verg. A. 11.483: praeses bellī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 364: president

    Lewis & Short: one that presides over, a president, superintendent, head (see president, of a country).

  • praesum, praeesse, praefuī — be at the head of, preside over

    verb, irregular, with the dative, conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.85: quī reī pūblicae praefutūrī sunt

    To be president of a society is societātī praeesse.

  • superintendēns, superintendentis m./f. — a superintendent (of a school district)

    declension · also used · modern · Traupman 388

Examples

  • maximārum societātum auctor, plūrimārum magister

    the founder of the biggest companies, and the president of a great manyCic. Planc. 32

See also president, society, organization, member.
